target.body:
## Summary

- plan repair validation as ordered, risk-aware proof stages and independently rebuild exact proof semantics before replay
- keep untrusted execution credential-free and lifecycle-script-free; bind immutable source, base, head, action, and output identities
- publish only exact independently validated commit and tree bytes through credential-scoped mutation jobs
- recheck live pause and structured security signals at every mutation boundary
- checkpoint replacement publication before irreversible source closeout and recover only the exact authorized replacement PR
- make retryable post-flight outcomes visible and durable for self-heal
- resolve rerun handoff artifacts by trusted producer artifact ID and digest instead of consumer attempt names
- reject unsafe command aliases and options, source mutation, proof drift, and terminal runtime budgets

## Final hardening

- revalidate every sealed issue and PR source in the shared guard immediately before privileged push/create/reopen/label/comment/close mutations
- allow source drift only for the exact prepared source head or a closure recorded by the verified publication checkpoint
- fail closed when a configured canonical changed-gate script disappears
- allow only narrow read-only package-manager proof forms; reject lifecycle, registry, and account mutations across pnpm, npm, Bun, and Yarn
- keep deadline-expired pending or missing checks retryable for durable self-heal
- snapshot ignored dependency/tooling inputs and symlink targets around every staged proof command
- verify every applicable strict ruleset, including bypass actors and the full effective required-check set
- bind issue-implementation readiness to the exact head in the verified publication receipt

target.title: feat(dashboard): add unlisted OpenClaw Bay demo
target.body:
## Summary

- add an unlisted, read-only OpenClaw Bay demo at `/bay-demo`
- turn the existing ClawSweeper status snapshot into an animated beach with live stage lanes, terminal pools, retrigger tunnels, repository filters, search, a detail drawer, master-sweeper modes, and a bounded 20-outcome tide rendered as a shoreline-following surge and backwash
- poll the shared Worker status 25% less often than Overview (every 20 seconds versus every 15 seconds), without adding a new GitHub API query path; actual upstream GitHub refreshes remain cache-dependent
- keep `/bay` unpublished and leave the existing Overview, issue-triage, and PR-proof-triage navigation unchanged

![OpenClaw Bay deterministic Playwright proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brokemac79/clawsweeper/62ce6243966a8c403eed095de33ba1f707967f47/docs/proof/openclaw-bay/playwright-proof-storyboard.jpg)

[Inspect the compact Playwright trace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brokemac79/clawsweeper/62ce6243966a8c403eed095de33ba1f707967f47/docs/proof/openclaw-bay/trace.zip) · [read the 23-assertion summary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brokemac79/clawsweeper/62ce6243966a8c403eed095de33ba1f707967f47/docs/proof/openclaw-bay/proof-summary.json) · [inspect the runner and exact fixtures](https://github.com/brokemac79/clawsweeper/tree/62ce6243966a8c403eed095de33ba1f707967f47/docs/proof/openclaw-bay)

## Problem

The operational Overview is intentionally dense and table-oriented. Maintainers asked to try a more visual, playful way to see whether ClawSweeper is active without replacing the existing operational surfaces. This PR publishes the selected prototype as an explicitly experimental demo on the existing dashboard Worker.

## Implementation

- renders active work in Arriving, Setting up, Reviewing, Repairing, and Applying lanes using the existing worker snapshot
- raises a READY flag and lets the master sweeper animate proved forward movement
- treats any new `run_id` for the same GitHub item as a retrigger, using the tunnel/re-emergence path even when a poll first sees the new run in the same or a later lane
- shows Completed, Failed, and Cancelled only from explicit terminal evidence; disappearing workers stay CHECKING during the bounded confirmation grace period
- stores only a bounded terminal view: fewer than 20 current outcomes, the latest 20 washed outcomes retained for the 60-second wash animation, and at most 256 seen event IDs under the existing seven-day status TTL
- adds `Where's my crustacean?`, repository filters, GitHub/workflow detail links, patrol/on-change modes, local-only tide preview, reduced-motion handling, and hardened noindex/no-store/frame-blocked headers
- replaces the prototype's flat tide overlay with a 7.2-second shoreline-following surge/recede animation built from inline SVG and CSS: translucent water and glass layers, painted sea texture, irregular foam, ripples, bubbles, wet-sand sheen, terminal-crustacean washout, and explicit incoming, crest, receding, and idle phases
- uses the same visible wash for preview and generated tides; a real tide commits the empty terminal buffer only after the crustaceans have moved seaward
- reuses the checked-in Bay background for water texture, announces tide state through a polite live region, and provides a brief static wash for reduced-motion users

## GitHub API And Runtime Load

Bay is a presentation over the existing cache-backed `/api/status` snapshot. It adds **no browser-to-GitHub requests and no new GitHub REST or GraphQL query path**. Terminal outcomes and timing samples are derived from workflow-job and recent-close data already collected for Overview.

Bay polls the Worker every 20 seconds versus Overview every 15 seconds: three rather than four status requests per minute after initial load, or 25% fewer browser-to-Worker requests. This is deliberately **not** described as 25% fewer upstream GitHub API calls: cache expiry, edge location, and concurrent viewers determine whether either status request causes a refresh. The defensible GitHub API claim is neutral/no-new-query-path, while browser polling load is lower.

The tide polish is presentation-only. It does not alter `/api/status`, its 20-second polling cadence, the Worker cache, status fields, or upstream GitHub collection, and it introduces no new external media or API request. It reuses the existing checked-in Bay background. The richer animation does have client-side rendering cost, so this is not a claim that Bay is lighter overall.

## Validation

- hosted CI on exact head `62ce6243966a8c403eed095de33ba1f707967f47` — `pnpm check`, Windows Codex launcher, both CodeQL analyses, and aggregate CodeQL passed
- `node --test test/dashboard-worker.test.ts` — 79/79 passed
- `node --test --test-name-pattern "OpenClaw Bay" test/dashboard-worker.test.ts` — 3/3 passed against the final exact-commit proof refresh
- `pnpm run build:dashboard` — passed
- `pnpm run lint:dashboard` — passed
- `node --check docs/proof/openclaw-bay/run-proof.mjs` — passed
- `pnpm exec oxlint docs/proof/openclaw-bay/run-proof.mjs --deny-warnings -D correctness` — passed
- `bash -n docs/proof/openclaw-bay/run-proof.sh` — passed with Git for Windows Bash
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check dashboard/bay-page.ts docs/proof/openclaw-bay/run-proof.mjs test/dashboard-worker.test.ts` — passed
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed
- local `pnpm check` reached the known Windows host baseline where shell-backed workflow tests call WSL `bash`; this machine's default `docker-desktop` distro has no `/bin/bash`. The changed dashboard build/lint/tests and Docker-backed browser proof pass; exact-head hosted CI is tracked below.

## Deterministic Browser Proof

The checked-in runner starts the real local Wrangler `/bay-demo` route and loads the real artwork. It replaces only `/api/status` with three exact synthetic, redacted transition responses plus one source-derived real-tide response, so the interactions are repeatable without credentials, live dashboard payloads, or GitHub API traffic.

Crabbox `local-container` proof `cbx_58b0a8f78e74` (`harbor-lobster`) used `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.60.0-noble` and passed all 23 assertions across 16 labelled frames:

- crustacean and master-sweeper animation clocks advance
- a forward transition raises READY, is physically swept, and lands in the reported lane
- a changed run ID creates both retrigger tunnel openings with the exact burrow label, then resurfaces in Setting up
- search focuses and highlights GitHub reference `#97722`
- repository filtering leaves only the selected repository's active and terminal items
- the detail drawer exposes exactly the safe GitHub item, job, and workflow-run links
- preview tide advances through incoming, crest, backwash, and restored states along the illustrated shoreline
- layered water, painted texture, irregular foam, ripples, bubbles, and wet-sand effects visibly wash the terminal pools
- terminal crustaceans disappear only at the temporary preview crest and return during backwash; preview sends no status poll or mutation and leaves terminal keys and `3 / 20` unchanged
- reduced-motion receives a bounded 520 ms static wash with the same non-mutating result
- a generated real tide visibly washes terminal crustaceans before committing the empty shared buffer; active-lane keys remain unchanged
- zero browser console errors, uncaught page errors, browser-to-`api.github.com` requests, or non-GET/HEAD requests

The three checked-in fixture bodies match their recorded SHA-256 values; the derived real-tide response has its own recorded SHA-256. A binary scan found no tokens, authorization headers, cookies, local Windows user paths, usernames, or live/private payloads. The final proof was generated against implementation commit `09941a121d0911278a64f71f3bbd7d57fa090dc8`; head `62ce6243966a8c403eed095de33ba1f707967f47` adds only the exact-commit proof refresh and source-SHA transport fallback.

## Review Closeout

- independent tide audit — accepted and fixed two findings: generated tides now animate terminal washout before clearing, and proof captures the visible incoming/crest/backwash states instead of the nearly transparent first 280 ms
- `codex review --uncommitted` — initial review accepted only stale proof/artifact hygiene findings; the checked-in 23-assertion evidence was regenerated and local Crabbox archives removed
- `codex review --uncommitted` — final implementation dirty review clean, no actionable findings
- exact-commit proof rerun — 23/23 Playwright assertions, 16 frames, zero direct GitHub API requests, zero mutation requests, unchanged preview keys, and a proved real clear
- `codex review --uncommitted` — proof-only refresh clean, no actionable findings
- `codex review --base origin/main` — final branch review clean; no actionable correctness issues, with dashboard build, focused tests, dashboard lint, and `git diff --check` passing

## Maintainer Decision

The product-boundary decision is resolved: @brokemac79 will own this experiment and accepts `/bay-demo` being unlisted and noindexed but unauthenticated and public by URL for the demo. `/bay` and the normal dashboard navigation remain unpublished.

This ownership decision does not make the route private. Anyone who knows or guesses the URL can open it; a genuinely maintainer-only deployment would still require Cloudflare Access or application authentication.

## Risks And Rollout

- `/bay-demo` is unlisted, not private. Anyone who knows or guesses the URL can open it; a maintainer-only rollout would need Cloudflare Access or separate application authentication.
- this is an experimental view, not a replacement for operational triage pages
- the terminal feed is intentionally bounded and evidence-based, so it is not a historical ledger
- inline page CSS/JS is allowed by the current route-specific CSP; external files or CSP nonces would be a later hardening improvement if the demo becomes permanent

## Release Note

Experimental: add an unlisted OpenClaw Bay dashboard demo that visualises the existing ClawSweeper worker state as an animated shoreline, including a layered shoreline-following tide and backwash.

target.title: fix(review): keep maturity labels out of issue lease revisions
target.body:
## Summary

- keep ClawSweeper-managed `maturity:stable` out of both issue source-revision implementations
- preserve revision changes for ordinary, protected, and `proof: override` labels
- cover the review/apply digest and the repair/router digest with matching focused tests

This prevents an exact issue review from invalidating its own apply-time mutation check after synchronizing the managed maturity label. It does not weaken exact-revision lease ownership, pull-request head-SHA coordination, human/protected-label drift detection, close safety, or security-label scanning.

## Original ClawSweeper patch vs maintainer follow-up

| | Original automated commit [`02bc535`](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/commit/02bc535958a75d35b41f448677d3ddb4060cb49f) | Maintainer follow-up [`bcdffe2`](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/commit/bcdffe2e0baec26f3be552e7812c61a871822bb1) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code | Updated only the review/apply predicate in `src/clawsweeper.ts`. | Also updates the parallel repair/router predicate in `src/repair/issue-source-guard.ts`. |
| Regression test | Added `maturity:stable` only to the review/apply digest fixture. | Adds it to the repair source-guard fixture and verifies both digest implementations remain identical. |
| Remaining risk | Fixed the observed self-CAS path, but left review and repair source revisions disagreeing whenever `maturity:stable` was present. Trusted close, comment-router, or issue-implementation guards could then reject a valid reviewed revision as changed. | Keeps both source-revision contracts aligned while retaining human/protected-label drift and security checks. |
| Incident explanation | Framed the symptom as a second worker missing a still-active first lease and attributed the affected path to PR #501. | Corrects the mechanism to first-run self-invalidation followed by normal failure retry, and traces the predicate to PR #371, maturity sync to PR #372, and enforcement to PR #462. |

The maintainer follow-up is two additional source/test lines beyond the original bot commit. It does not change concurrency groups, lease election, retry policy, GitHub permissions, or close behavior.

## Actual production problem

The bug was not two concurrent workers failing to honor the same active lease.

The first exact review of an issue can validate its source revision, add ClawSweeper-owned labels, and then validate the revision again. Priority and impact labels were already revision-neutral, but `maturity:stable` was not. Adding it changed `itemSourceRevisionSha256`, so the same worker failed with:

```text
issue source revision changed while holding the apply mutation lease
```

Failure reconciliation then returned the original `issues/opened` queue item to pending. A later run legitimately acquired a new lease and posted another review-start placeholder. The two workers did not overlap.

For openclaw/openclaw#104977:

- [run 29180589969](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29180589969) checked out `a7edd3f`, posted the first start marker at 2026-07-12 05:04:20 UTC, added `maturity:stable` at 05:12:08, and rejected its own revision at 05:12:10
- the run failed and completed at 05:12:17
- retry [run 29180841398](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29180841398) was created at 05:12:54, posted a new start marker at 05:14:04, and succeeded

Independent end-to-end examples show the same `maturity:stable` → two-to-three-second CAS rejection → successful retry sequence on openclaw/openclaw#104972, #104979, and #104984. The behavior also predates the July 12 cache/concurrency merges; [run 29085983494](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29085983494) reproduced it on July 10.

## Implementation

- `src/clawsweeper.ts`: use the authoritative `MATURITY_LABEL_NAMES` set in the review/apply advisory-label predicate
- `src/repair/issue-source-guard.ts`: apply the same policy in trusted close, comment-router, and issue-implementation source guards
- add `maturity:stable` to both existing source-revision regression fixtures

Updating both implementations is required. A review-only change made the review digest stable but left the repair digest different for the same labeled issue.

## Validation

- `pnpm run build`
- `pnpm run build:repair`
- `node --test test/review-comment-rendering.test.ts test/repair/issue-source-guard.test.ts test/apply-label-sync.test.ts test/repair/comment-router-core.test.ts` — 170/170 passed
- cross-module digest probe — review/apply and repair/router digests both remain stable and identical after adding `maturity:stable`
- `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD`
- `codex review --uncommitted` — clean after the accepted repair/router alignment finding
- `codex review --base origin/main` — clean: “The maturity label is consistently excluded from both review and repair source-revision hashes, with focused coverage passing.”
- exact-head [GitHub Actions CI](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29190737572) and [CodeQL](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29190737579) — passed
- exact-head [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/510#issuecomment-4950254782) — ready for maintainer review, 🦀 challenger crab

`pnpm run check` on native Windows passed active-surface checks, limits, all builds, and all lint phases, then reached unrelated existing test-fixture prerequisites (`bash` via a non-Linux WSL default distro and Windows symlink permissions). No platform/test-harness files were changed. Fresh GitHub Actions CI on the exact head is the authoritative aggregate Linux gate.

## Provenance

- [PR #372](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/372), merged as `82a1bfda0da5490be8a2d90a3d26bef3f29d8509` on 2026-06-26, introduced managed `maturity:stable` synchronization
- [PR #371](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/371), merged afterward as `84796f0c9b0c04bbed1476251ff2b1465701a915`, introduced issue source-revision hashing and the parallel advisory-label predicates without maturity, creating the latent mismatch
- [PR #462](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/462), merged as `d43deab4b78d0e58ecc7525cef175106b2fc559d` on 2026-07-10, added exact issue/apply mutation enforcement and made the mismatch fail visibly
